# Mesh recipe portability fixtures

`legacy.json` was generated by native Python using the frozen pre-recipe kernel
with its original, all-property-break `asw.py`. It was not made by deleting
metadata from a current mesh. `current.json` was generated by the current
`physical-breaks-v1` recipe. Each contains an unloaded steady capture, material
mesh arrays, and two accepted steps for both BDF2 and Radau. The imposed lateral
acceleration gives a nonzero 0.004 m/s final frame velocity.

`PROVENANCE.json` pins these files and records the historical source locations.
Each payload also pins every producer module and records native residual and
accepted-method replay results. Historical local paths document generation;
they are not dependencies of the portability test.

Run the focused test from the repository root:

```sh
node scripts/test-mesh-recipe-wasm.mjs
```

It loads the local `public/runtime` Pyodide runtime and current `openswing`
source, then restores the frozen native packets at their original states.
Set `OPENSWING_RESULTS` to a JSON path to retain its report. It does not run
new time integrations in WASM or replace the fixture packets.

Fixture regeneration is explicit. `generate.py --kernel-parent PATH --recipe
legacy|current` imports the selected kernel directory, verifies that its source
hashes remain unchanged, and writes only the selected native payload. Replacing
the historical fixture with current output would remove its historical-producer
coverage and is not a routine test update.
